stops.title: Why a bad line used to poison every total
stops.summary: Context only. `parseRate` split each CSV line and called `Number` on the value, so a line without a number gave `value: NaN`, and `total` returned `NaN` for the whole file.

stops.title: Bad lines become `null` instead of a `NaN` rate
stops.summary: `parseRate` now returns `null` for a line with no currency or no number, and trims the currency. The return type says so: `Rate | null`.

attention.note: Every caller of `parseRate` must now handle `null`. `mapRates` is the only caller in this repo.

excerpts.caption: The parser refuses a line it cannot read
A line without a number parses to `null`

files.note: One new case for a line with no number

notes.title: An empty currency counts as bad
notes.body: A line like `,12` splits into an empty currency, which is falsy.

questions: Should a bad line be reported, not just skipped?

stops.title: The total loop becomes a reduce
stops.summary: `total` sums with `reduce` instead of a hand-written loop. Behaviour is the same for any list of rates.

attention.note: The reduce is shorter but hides the running sum from a debugger. Decide whether that matters here.

notes.title: Starts at zero
notes.body: An empty list still totals `0`, as before.

stops.title: The README says what happens to bad lines
stops.summary: One sentence: the reader skips lines it cannot parse.

attention.note: Skipped lines are silent. A file full of typos totals `0` with no warning.

questions: Should the CLI print how many lines it skipped?
